takeaways: Rising 30-year Treasury yields and institutional warnings of an AI-driven equity bubble signal a shift toward risk-off sentiment as investors demand higher compensation for persistent inflation and debt.
The AI infrastructure boom is fueled by massive, debt-heavy capital expenditures and creative financing, raising concerns about corporate leverage and the sustainability of long-term profitability.
China’s economy faces a structural 'strong supply, weak demand' imbalance, where high-tech manufacturing growth masks deep-seated fragility in the property sector and domestic balance sheets.
day_verdict: Major day — market-moving events; read carefully.

items.title: AI market correction is coming, ECB blog predicts
bullets: The European Central Bank has issued a formal warning suggesting that the current valuation levels in the artificial intelligence sector may be unsustainable, signaling a potential market correction.

Investors should prepare for increased volatility as central bank oversight of AI-driven equity bubbles intensifies, potentially impacting capital allocation strategies in technology-heavy portfolios.
items.reason: Systemic risk warning from a major central bank regarding AI valuations.

items.title: Ditch inflation targets? Better to overhaul them instead
bullets: Global central banks are facing mounting pressure to modernize inflation targeting frameworks as structural shifts like AI, supply chain disruptions, and geopolitical shocks render traditional 2% targets increasingly difficult to maintain.

The analysis suggests that while abandoning targets would destabilize inflation expectations, authorities must improve transparency by articulating alternative policy scenarios to better manage market uncertainty.
items.reason: Fundamental shift in global monetary policy strategy and expectations.

items.title: Sri Lankan inflation to slow towards goal, central bank head says
bullets: Sri Lanka's central bank leadership anticipates a deceleration in inflation, signaling a potential stabilization of the country's macroeconomic environment following recent periods of extreme volatility.
This projected trend toward the official inflation target provides a positive indicator for emerging market investors monitoring the recovery trajectory of debt-distressed economies in South Asia.
items.reason: Regional economic update with limited impact on global markets.

items.title: Stock Market Today, Aug. 17: Markets Inch Lower and Treasury Yields Rise as Investors Wait for Retail Earnings
bullets: The U.S. 30-year Treasury yield reached 5.3%, its highest level since 2007, signaling heightened investor caution as the market awaits critical earnings reports from major retailers like Walmart, Home Depot, and Target.

While major indices like the S&P 500 and Dow Jones drifted lower, the market remains near record highs, with current price action reflecting a 'risk-off' sentiment as participants weigh the impact of rising bond yields on growth and AI-related stocks.
items.reason: Captures critical macroeconomic shifts in bond yields and market sentiment ahead of key earnings.

items.title: Billionaire investor Leon Cooperman sees a recession in 2027 and a stock drop ahead
bullets: Prominent investor Leon Cooperman has issued a bearish outlook, forecasting a potential economic recession by 2027 that could trigger a significant downturn in equity valuations.

This outlook highlights growing institutional concern regarding the sustainability of current market highs, suggesting that long-term investors should prepare for a period of volatility as economic headwinds potentially materialize in the coming years.
items.reason: Provides a notable contrarian institutional perspective on long-term market stability.

items.title: US Bond Selloff Drives 30-Year Yields to Highest Since 2007
bullets: The 30-year US Treasury yield reached 5.29%, marking its highest level since 2007, as investors demand higher compensation for persistent inflation and mounting national debt concerns.
Recent Treasury auctions have struggled, with the 30-year bond auction yield hitting 5.216%, the highest level since 2001, signaling waning demand for long-dated government debt.
items.reason: Benchmark yield surge impacting global borrowing costs

items.title: US stocks fall on spiking bond yields, higher oil prices
bullets: Geopolitical instability in the Strait of Hormuz has pushed oil prices up by over two percent, exacerbating inflationary pressures and creating a significant headwind for equity markets.

The European Central Bank has issued warnings regarding potential spillover effects from a US-centric AI equity bubble, suggesting that a correction could negatively impact euro area sentiment and financing conditions.
items.reason: Geopolitical risk and cross-asset market contagion

items.title: China’s Economy Is Not Collapsing. It Is Being Rolled Over.
bullets: Official data reveals a stark structural divergence: while overall GDP grew 4.7% in the first half of 2026, real-estate investment plummeted 18.0%, signaling a deep-seated contraction in the traditional property-led growth model.

The economy is currently defined by a 'strong supply, weak demand' imbalance, where 13.3% growth in high-tech manufacturing and 13.4% export growth are masking the underlying fragility of domestic balance sheets and fixed-asset investment.
items.reason: Provides a critical, data-backed assessment of China's structural economic transition.

items.title: China House Price Index Shows Slower Decline in July, Improving to -3.2%
bullets: The residential property price index improved marginally to -3.2% in July from -3.3% in June, marking two consecutive months of slight stabilization despite the sector remaining in deep contraction territory.

While government stimulus measures like lower mortgage rates and purchase easing are in effect, the recovery remains fragile as developer defaults and unsold inventory continue to severely weigh on consumer confidence and household wealth.
items.reason: Highlights a potential inflection point in the property sector, a key drag on Chinese growth.

items.title: MTR profit more than doubles to $15.9b in H1 on property gains
bullets: MTR Corporation reported a 105.9% year-on-year surge in net profit to HK$15.87 billion, primarily driven by a 120.7% increase in property development profits from projects like Tai Wai Station and THE SOUTHSIDE.

While property gains bolstered the bottom line, recurrent business profit grew by only 1.3%, and total revenue declined by 4.1%, highlighting a heavy reliance on property cycles rather than core transport operations.
items.reason: Significant earnings report from a major infrastructure and property developer.

items.title: URA swings to $338m surplus after three years of losses
bullets: The Urban Renewal Authority (URA) returned to an operating surplus of HK$338 million in the 2025/26 fiscal year, ending a three-year streak of net losses that saw deficits as high as HK$3.92 billion.

The turnaround follows significant strategic adjustments and resource management in response to property market volatility, with the government now reviewing the URA's financial and operational models to ensure long-term sustainability.
items.reason: Indicates stabilization in the government-backed urban development sector.

items.title: Why Big Tech’s AI Spending Is $3 Trillion Higher Than It Seems
bullets: Reports indicate that major technology firms are concealing approximately $3 trillion in AI-related expenditures, significantly altering the perceived capital intensity of the current AI infrastructure build-out.

This massive hidden spending suggests that the financial burden of achieving AI dominance is far greater than public balance sheets reflect, potentially impacting future earnings expectations and free cash flow projections for investors.
items.reason: Significant revaluation of Big Tech capital expenditure and financial health.

items.title: Tech companies’ AI debt surges as Oracle nears junk credit rating
bullets: The aggressive pursuit of AI infrastructure is driving a surge in corporate debt levels across the technology sector, with Oracle specifically facing the risk of a downgrade to junk status.

Rising leverage ratios in the tech industry signal increasing financial vulnerability, as companies borrow heavily to fund capital-intensive AI projects that have yet to demonstrate consistent, long-term profitability.
items.reason: Indicates systemic credit risk and financial strain from AI investment cycles.

items.title: Nvidia backing $105 billion in financing for OpenAI data center in Ohio
bullets: Nvidia is providing up to $105 billion in financing for an OpenAI data center in Ohio, which will support an initial 4.25 gigawatts of computing capacity with potential for expansion to 8 gigawatts.

The project involves a 20-year lease with SB Energy and includes a $4.2 billion investment in regional grid infrastructure, highlighting the massive capital expenditure required to secure the 'new oil' of the AI age.
items.reason: Major capital commitment signaling long-term infrastructure scaling.

items.title: Executives put the spotlight on AI’s reliability issue
bullets: A survey of over 100 C-suite executives reveals that only 33% believe AI consistently delivers intended outcomes, while just 16% trust autonomous AI for critical business operations.

The findings suggest a shift toward more cautious, pragmatic AI deployment as enterprises struggle with high costs, low workforce adoption, and the difficulty of proving business value beyond technical metrics.
items.reason: Highlights critical enterprise adoption hurdles and ROI skepticism.

items.title: Nvidia to provide up to $105 billion guarantee for OpenAI's Ohio data center
bullets: Nvidia is spearheading a massive infrastructure project in Ohio, providing a financial guarantee of up to $105 billion to support a new data center facility where OpenAI will serve as the primary tenant under a 20-year lease.

The facility is designed to scale up to 8 gigawatts of power, with the initial deployment exclusively utilizing Nvidia hardware, signaling a strategic effort by the chipmaker to secure long-term, high-volume demand for its compute products.
items.reason: Major capital commitment and strategic lock-in with a key AI customer.

items.title: Nvidia financing initiative follows SEC guidance that takes sponsors off the hook for data center investments
bullets: Recent SEC staff opinion has effectively exempted certain data center debt from Dodd-Frank risk retention rules, allowing Nvidia and its financial partners to structure more flexible and capital-efficient financing for AI infrastructure.

This regulatory shift facilitates a broader $500 billion push into AI asset-backed securities, enabling Nvidia to offload risk while accelerating the deployment of its hardware through creative, debt-fueled capital structures.
items.reason: Regulatory tailwinds significantly lower the barrier for massive AI infrastructure financing.

items.title: Geely to Build Cars at Volvo’s European Plants From 2028, New Chairman Says
bullets: Geely plans to utilize Volvo's existing European manufacturing facilities in Sweden, Belgium, and Slovakia to produce high-end and luxury vehicles starting in 2028.
This strategic move aims to circumvent steep EU tariffs on imported Chinese electric vehicles while simultaneously optimizing Volvo's spare production capacity and supply chain coordination.
items.reason: Strategic manufacturing shift to mitigate trade barriers and improve operational efficiency.

items.title: Europe’s subsidy-driven growth lifts global EV sales 9% in July
bullets: Global EV sales reached 1.85 million units in July 2026, with Europe acting as the primary growth engine through a 33% year-on-year increase fueled by aggressive regional subsidy schemes.

The market remains highly fragmented, as North American sales slumped 27% year-on-year due to the expiration of federal incentives, highlighting the critical dependence of EV adoption on government policy support.
items.reason: Highlights the critical impact of government subsidies on regional EV demand and global market divergence.

items.title: PJM’s New Deal for Data Centers: Bring Power or Face Cuts
bullets: PJM Interconnection has proposed a new reliability framework to FERC that would allow large data centers to enter service before sufficient grid capacity is fully available, provided they secure their own power.

Facilities failing to back their peak demand with qualifying new capacity face potential emergency curtailment, introducing significant operational risk and capital requirements for developers operating within the PJM region.
items.reason: Regulatory shift impacting data center viability and operational risk in the US's largest grid.

items.title: Jabil Rides on AI Data Center Boom: Is More Growth Ahead?
bullets: Jabil projects AI-related revenue to reach $13.6 billion in fiscal 2026, a substantial increase from $9 billion in the prior year, driven by end-to-end infrastructure demand including networking and cooling.

The company is actively scaling manufacturing capacity across the US, Mexico, and India while exploring a multi-gigawatt strategic alliance with Adani Enterprise to capture long-term growth in the AI rack and server market.
items.reason: Quantifiable revenue growth and strategic expansion in the critical AI hardware supply chain.

items.title: Satellite operators emphasize launch deals in a constrained market
bullets: Satellite operators are increasingly securing launch capacity years in advance to mitigate industry-wide supply constraints, with AST SpaceMobile reporting 10 launches booked across two providers to support its constellation deployment.

The grounding of Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket following a May explosion has forced operators to rely heavily on SpaceX’s Falcon 9, creating a bottleneck as Falcon 9’s lower payload capacity necessitates more frequent launches to meet deployment targets.
items.reason: Highlights critical supply chain bottlenecks impacting the commercial satellite sector.

items.title: China bounces back from Long March rocket explosion with back-to-back launches
bullets: CASC successfully resumed operations with two launches within 24 hours following the August 10 failure of a Long March 7A, suggesting the anomaly was not systemic to the YF-100 engine family used across multiple Chinese launch vehicles.

The rapid return to flight mitigates potential long-term disruption to China's Guowang megaconstellation and GEO launch schedules, though the Long March 7A remains grounded pending a full investigation into the structural failure.
items.reason: Demonstrates resilience in China's space program despite recent high-profile launch failures.
